findings.title: Messages have no intent consumer
findings.finding: Delivery stores the message and recipient rows. _messaging.pending exists, but the production controller/execution loop does not call it. No production path consumes a chief inbox into a planning turn.
findings.consequence: Chat can acknowledge and display messages while producing no reply or work.

findings.title: Public task creation stops at draft
findings.finding: task.create persists draft; task.assign changes worker/version without readying it. The current public catalog has no task.start. The first-task test explicitly asserts draft. Internal scheduling can ready generated tasks, so readiness itself is not entirely absent.
findings.consequence: A publicly created first task has no normal public transition into executable work.

findings.title: Hosted runs are not automatically claimed
findings.finding: readyScan only counts tasks. _execution.tick expires leases and admits already claimed attempts with a ContextArtifact. It does not claim queued hosted runs.
findings.consequence: Even ready scheduled work does not initiate a hosted attempt by itself.

findings.title: Context assembler is absent
findings.finding: run.claim can return a digest-only synthetic input envelope; _execution.context records a supplied artifact but no production caller builds and publishes the actual transcript/tool/memory context.
findings.consequence: No assembled authorized model input reaches a hosted worker.

findings.title: Prepared model action is incompatible with the implemented adapter
findings.finding: Execution emits attempt_id/run_id/model parameters, empty content, tool=profile.ID and connection.version=1. Responses requires schema/kind/context_artifact/max_output_tokens/tool_contract_versions and rejects unknown fields. Controller infers callback routing from attempt_id in those same parameters.
findings.consequence: Simply registering Responses still produces invalid actions; removing the illegal parameters would also lose the current callback route.

findings.title: Model output is not converted into actions or a final result
findings.finding: handleObservation records observations and increments a counter, then prepares another model effect on succeeded or accepted until the bound. It does not consume text/tool_proposals, publish a chief reply, invoke local product operations, or report final outputs.
findings.consequence: The central intent-to-work step is unbuilt. A model call alone cannot run a workflow.

findings.title: Responses is implemented but not wired
findings.finding: Startup constructors register github/httpread/serenity only; responses is still explicitly listed as unimplemented although its package and tests exist. A responses.json profile is rejected as an unknown adapter.
findings.consequence: Production cannot use its existing model adapter.

findings.title: Verification has no production driver
findings.finding: Reports create rows in execution_verification_jobs. NewVerifier and _execution.verification.record exist, but controller has no verifier phase/caller or pending verification scan, and entrypoint attaches only Identity and Blobs.
findings.consequence: Reported work cannot automatically become independently verified success.

findings.title: Generated-output acceptance is not connected end to end
findings.finding: Presence checks demand an expected digest at task admission, while report builds VerificationRequest.Outputs as an empty array. Verifier addresses artifacts by expected digest rather than resolving the attempt output name.
findings.consequence: A newly generated report cannot be verified by its named output contract without prior knowledge or a workaround.

findings.title: Repository verification runner is unbuilt
findings.finding: Repository patch/check observation kinds fall into an unavailable result explaining the controlled runner is absent. Artifact presence/digest/schema checks do exist.
findings.consequence: Engineering tasks cannot establish independent patch/check acceptance.

findings.title: Durable local jobs have no production runners
findings.finding: Jobs without a registered exact owner/operation runner remain pending; production registers no Jobs map. skill.evaluate and run.export create such work.
findings.consequence: These public operations can return a durable identity without ever producing their result.

findings.title: Configuration exports return unregistered result identities
findings.finding: handleExport stages/publishes bytes inside the handler and constructs succeeded Job and Artifact IDs locally; it does not persist them through execution/artifacts owners.
findings.consequence: Returned job/artifact references have no demonstrated owner-backed lookup/read lifecycle; writer transaction also contains blob IO.

findings.title: Reconciliation cannot reach Adapter.Reconcile
findings.finding: operation.reconcile creates an execution job referring to the original operation_id. Generic jobs treat linked effects as externally completed, while dispatch skips unknown/awaiting-confirmation originals. Production physical invocation calls Invoke; no controller caller invokes Reconcile.
findings.consequence: Unknown/accepted effects have no complete runtime lookup/confirmation path.

findings.title: Responsibility cycles never feed back their next decision
findings.finding: Wake admission creates a cycle task and deliberately leaves the next wake for _scheduling.cycle.record. There is no production execution caller that interprets the cycle and records it.
findings.consequence: An ongoing responsibility does not autonomously reason, spawn useful work and schedule its next reconsideration.

findings.title: Credential setup ends at a helper contract without a shipped producer
findings.finding: Connections verifies signed helper receipts using a provisioned receipt key and a resolvable credential reference. Packaging validates secure-helper metadata. No production helper implementation/entrypoint producing this setup handoff was found in the executable tree.
findings.consequence: The operator cannot complete the intended secret-free onboarding solely through the advertised product flow.

findings.title: Serenity is a capability-refusal adapter, not working memory
findings.finding: The pinned capability report declares physical_calls=none and unsupported command lookup; adapter operations refuse required missing guarantees rather than making requests. Local memory bindings/jobs exist.
findings.consequence: Real recall/curation/promotion/context memory and full memory backup require a qualified upstream seam, not just wiring.

findings.title: Backup captures database bytes but omits required content
findings.finding: Backup genuinely captures/encrypts database bytes. Manifest schema versions, artifacts, brains and retained obligations are empty lists; these are required for complete installation recovery.
findings.consequence: A valid encrypted bundle is not yet a complete portable installation backup.

findings.title: Restore prepares an overlay but never rewinds the live installation
findings.finding: Restore validates a bundle and stages a recovery overlay; comments explicitly defer file replacement to controller. No production restore coordinator is wired. Integration test ends accepted/paused, not after restored data is read. The overlay also needs complete monotonic records, not only obligation summaries.
findings.consequence: Restore remains an incomplete job; clean-destination artifact/key/brain restoration and revocation preservation are not demonstrated.

findings.title: Desktop chat contract lacks persistent complete history
findings.finding: Desktop combines incoming mailbox and this window’s sent messages; catalog lacks full thread history/current caller/read-state projections. Local UI cache is in-memory; restart persistence is not implemented in the inspected client.
findings.consequence: Relaunch cannot show a reliable complete conversation, unread state or retained offline draft.

findings.title: Desktop management and detail journeys are incomplete
findings.finding: The live client honestly renders notices for unlistable memory and absent history/provenance/check projections. New org/worker/task/responsibility creation flows and populated daily-work behavior are not complete production journeys.
findings.consequence: A rendered chat shell is not the specified daily work application.

findings.title: Qualification has unconditional not-run branches
findings.finding: Responses qualification always calls notRun even when Go source exists. Desktop cases always notRun even if a driver appears. Distribution tests always notRun after host checks. Named-agent sessions are correctly opt-in. Baseline observed 14 skipped test/subtest events.
findings.consequence: A green go test run does not mean these release gates are satisfied. Some need harness code, others real authorized environments.

findings.title: Parity tests cover a small script, not all behavioral lifecycles
findings.finding: Current parity script has nine calls largely covering installation/principal operations. Discovery tests enumerate the whole surface, but that is not all-operation success/state/recovery parity or end-to-end work. Many controller unit tests use fake owners.
findings.consequence: Package-local green tests can miss incompatible runtime seams and missing transitions.

findings.title: Release library exists but no installable product is qualified
findings.finding: Packaging implements manifests, signing, install plans, services and desktop archives against synthetic trees. It lacks a completed artifact-production/clean-host lifecycle, and qualification workflow intentionally does not publish.
findings.consequence: Distribution/helper/service/keychain behavior remains coding plus real platform qualification work.

findings.title: Documentation and dependency evidence are stale
findings.finding: README says no runnable implementation; index calls this only a scaffold; lock lists old Fyne qualification; Responses startup comments are stale. Some desktop notes describe defects now covered by passing regression tests.
findings.consequence: New implementers could rebuild working packages or carry obsolete assumptions forward.

findings.title: Root budgets and authority need real-loop integration proof
findings.finding: Task/attempt/effect reservations and current authority exist independently. The missing hosted path has not demonstrated their combined semantics, worker identity intersection, current revocation and unknown cost settlement.
findings.consequence: Naively adding a planner could bypass authorization or double-reserve/spend; preserve existing code and test the integrated path.

findings.title: Recovery/fairness edges need explicit coverage
findings.finding: Controller documents a stranded claim when a lost claim acknowledgement cannot be resolved through pending reads. Several pending scans are limited batches without a complete fair work cursor; starvation under many blocked records needs a reproducer.
findings.consequence: Recovery and long-running installations can stall even after the happy path is wired.

findings.title: Responses performs two physical requests in one dispatch
findings.finding: Invoke can create a conversation and then call Responses before returning one observation. This violates the frozen one-physical-call dispatch expectation and leaves the session-handle handoff inside adapter IO. Checked-in protocol notes correctly say an empty conversation cannot prove nonexecution and reconciled items do not recover billing usage.
findings.consequence: Crash accounting, call-count guarantees and uncertainty need a coordinated contract/runtime repair; a successful API-key probe does not establish them.
